scenarios.name: clock-record-0_5x
scenarios.description: A 0.5x take runs east for its whole 1-bar allowance (120 local ticks) and is then resolved; the world advances 8 substeps per local tick.

scenarios.name: clock-record-1x
scenarios.description: A 1x take runs east for its whole 1-bar allowance (120 local ticks) and is then resolved; the world advances 4 substeps per local tick.

scenarios.name: clock-record-2x
scenarios.description: A 2x take runs east for its whole 1-bar allowance (120 local ticks) and is then resolved; the world advances 2 substeps per local tick.

scenarios.name: clock-record-4x
scenarios.description: A 4x take runs east for its whole 1-bar allowance (120 local ticks) and is then resolved; the world advances 1 substeps per local tick.

scenarios.name: clock-plate-2x-record-replay
scenarios.description: A 2x take lands on a plate; the plate event happens at the same master substep in recording and in replay.

scenarios.name: record-busy-death
scenarios.description: Record-then-resolve fidelity: a busy 1x take (switch, door, plate, grunt, turret) dies part-way; the replay reproduces positions, kills and the death.

scenarios.name: record-two-takes-busy
scenarios.description: Take A (2x, busy script) is recorded, then take B (1x, reverse) is recorded live against A; the combined run is resolved.

scenarios.name: record-calm-kill-win
scenarios.description: A surviving take waits for an awake grunt and kills it with a standing 1x light; recording and replay agree exactly and the run wins.

scenarios.name: mech-dead-signal-opens-door
scenarios.description: A standing 1x light kills a sleeping one-hit grunt; the door wired to dead:g1 starts opening on the next mechanisms update.

scenarios.name: clock-empty-run
scenarios.description: No tapes at all (after a reset): the encounter runs to the horizon with no selves and fails with no survivor.

scenarios.name: tapemode-stop
scenarios.description: A 2x 'stop' tape (1 bar, horizon 2 bars) walks to a switch and a turret, toggles and swings; end behaviour applies against a world that keeps going.

scenarios.name: tapemode-repeat
scenarios.description: A 2x 'repeat' tape (1 bar, horizon 2 bars) walks to a switch and a turret, toggles and swings; end behaviour applies against a world that keeps going.

scenarios.name: tapemode-reverse
scenarios.description: A 2x 'reverse' tape (1 bar, horizon 2 bars) walks to a switch and a turret, toggles and swings; end behaviour applies against a world that keeps going.

scenarios.name: tapemode-mixed-four
scenarios.description: Four tapes at once, one per speed (0.5x stop, 1x repeat, 2x reverse, 4x repeat), striking one tough turret and toggling a switch; traversals, wraps and turns interleave.

scenarios.name: tapemode-record-4x-reverse
scenarios.description: A 4x reverse take is recorded from inputs (one world substep per local tick), toggling a switch; the resolution ping-pongs it eight times over the horizon.

scenarios.name: ghost-scenario-c
scenarios.description: Scenario C: the take is shot early, keeps going as a recording ghost (strikes the grunt, flips the lever, walks through the door); replayed, it dies again and none of that happens.

scenarios.name: ghost-recghost-blocked-by-door
scenarios.description: The recording ghost is still blocked by a closed door (the door here never opens).

scenarios.name: ghost-rescue
scenarios.description: Rescue: take B (2x) destroys the turret before its first shot, so take A survives and its later strike and lever become effective; both survive and win.

scenarios.name: ghost-scenario-d-alone
scenarios.description: Scenario D control: tape A alone survives the corridor and lights the lamp.

scenarios.name: ghost-scenario-d
scenarios.description: Scenario D: tape B opens the door late, exposing A to the turret; A dies at a new time, keeps moving as a ghost, its lamp switch does not count, and B wins alone.

scenarios.name: survivors-one-wins
scenarios.description: Three selves burn in a laser; the fourth kills the grunt and survives: the attempt is won with one survivor.

scenarios.name: survivors-none-fails
scenarios.description: The objective completes but every self dies afterwards: not a win (reason noSurvivor).

scenarios.name: ghost-final-tape-edge
scenarios.description: Final-tape edge case: take B dies in a laser, then as a recording ghost kills the grunt (the provisional run latches the objective); the authoritative resolve does not.

scenarios.name: desync-scenario-i-detour
scenarios.description: Scenario I: a door closes across the runner, which desyncs; its spark takes the open detour at finite speed and resyncs on catch-up; the runner then holds the exit.

scenarios.name: desync-scenario-i-reopened
scenarios.description: Scenario I: the switcher reopens the direct route at tick 150, so the spark catches up sooner than by the detour.

scenarios.name: desync-no-route
scenarios.description: With no route the spark never catches up; nothing teleports or kills it; the alive-but-desynced self is a survivor that cannot hold the exit.

scenarios.name: desync-route-reopened-by-other
scenarios.description: Another tape reopens the blocked route at tick 300; the spark recovers and the run wins.

scenarios.name: desync-repeat-cut-spark
scenarios.description: A 2x repeat runner desyncs at the closed door; at the cut the projection teleports back to the start but the spark has to travel, then resyncs with the new traversal.

scenarios.name: desync-harmless-invulnerable
scenarios.description: A self desynced on a low barrier swings at a grunt for no damage; the turret ignores it and shoots the self standing behind it, straight through the projection.

scenarios.name: desync-scenario-j-control
scenarios.description: Scenario J control: without desync the turret kills the crossing tape in its lane.

scenarios.name: desync-scenario-j
scenarios.description: Scenario J: desync protects the crossing, the spark detours, the tape resyncs behind the turret and breaks it.

scenarios.name: desync-scenario-j-no-detour
scenarios.description: TEST-17: the spark never catches up, so the desynced strike cannot hurt the turret.

scenarios.name: enemy-grunt-strike
scenarios.description: A grunt walks at the only self and strikes on its beat grid after a telegraph; one strike kills; the ghost is never targeted again.

scenarios.name: enemy-grunt-target-switch
scenarios.description: A closer self (B) changes the grunt’s target on a beat boundary while A’s path is unchanged.

scenarios.name: combat-knockback-alone-whiff
scenarios.description: Knockback control: alone, A’s swing at an empty spot whiffs.

scenarios.name: combat-knockback-changes-later-hit
scenarios.description: B knocks the grunt east into the spot where A swings later; the same recorded swing now kills.

scenarios.name: momentum-0_5x-stand
scenarios.description: One light swing at a tough sleeping grunt from a 0.5x tape, standing: momentum sets damage, knockback and stagger.

scenarios.name: momentum-1x-stand
scenarios.description: One light swing at a tough sleeping grunt from a 1x tape, standing: momentum sets damage, knockback and stagger.

scenarios.name: momentum-2x-stand
scenarios.description: One light swing at a tough sleeping grunt from a 2x tape, standing: momentum sets damage, knockback and stagger.

scenarios.name: momentum-1x-into
scenarios.description: One light swing at a tough sleeping grunt from a 1x tape, moving into the strike: momentum sets damage, knockback and stagger.

scenarios.name: momentum-1x-away
scenarios.description: One light swing at a tough sleeping grunt from a 1x tape, moving away from the strike: momentum sets damage, knockback and stagger.

scenarios.name: dodge-iframes-pass-through
scenarios.description: A bolt arriving inside the dodge’s i-frames passes through and breaks on the wall behind.

scenarios.name: dodge-too-early-dies
scenarios.description: The same dodge started far too early: its i-frames are over when the bolt arrives, which kills.

scenarios.name: dodge-record-live-iframes
scenarios.description: A recorded dodge gives the live self the same i-frames (10 local ticks) during recording.

scenarios.name: momentum-wall-1x-stand-light
scenarios.description: Scenario K: a 1x standing light clangs (momentum 1.2 of 5).

scenarios.name: momentum-wall-1x-run-heavy
scenarios.description: Scenario K: a 1x running heavy is still too weak (momentum 3).

scenarios.name: momentum-wall-2x-stand-heavy
scenarios.description: Scenario K: a 2x standing heavy is still too weak (momentum 4).

scenarios.name: momentum-wall-2x-run-heavy
scenarios.description: Scenario K: a 2x running heavy breaks it (momentum 6) and the self walks through the gap.

scenarios.name: mech-door-closes-on-playback
scenarios.description: A door closing on a playback self desyncs it (doors never delete a body); the spark starts beside the door.

scenarios.name: mech-door-closes-on-live
scenarios.description: A door closing on the live self pushes it out to the nearest free side; it stays alive and synced.

scenarios.name: mech-door-pushes-enemy
scenarios.description: A door closing on a sleeping grunt pushes it out of the doorway.

scenarios.name: mech-interact-nothing
scenarios.description: An interact with nothing in reach emits interactFail "nothing in reach".

scenarios.name: mech-plate-holds-laser-off
scenarios.description: An effective body holds a plate, which switches a laser off for another self crossing it.

scenarios.name: mech-laser-kills
scenarios.description: Without the plate held the laser kills the crossing self (fail with no survivor).

scenarios.name: ability-laser-proof
scenarios.description: laserProof: the same crossing survives the live laser.

scenarios.name: mech-heavy-plate-needs-heavystep
scenarios.description: A heavy plate ignores an ordinary self.

scenarios.name: ability-heavy-step
scenarios.description: heavyStep: the same self holds the heavy plate and turns the laser off.

scenarios.name: mech-dead-ghost-no-plate
scenarios.description: A self dies to a laser on the way; its ghost then stands on the plate, which stays off.

scenarios.name: objective-reach-win
scenarios.description: reach: an alive, synced self is in the exit when the horizon ends (the objective latches on the last substep).

scenarios.name: objective-reach-pass-by-fails
scenarios.description: reach: passing through the exit and leaving again does not count.

scenarios.name: objective-core-weak-clang
scenarios.description: activate: a 0.5x light (momentum 0.6) clangs off a threshold-1 core.

scenarios.name: objective-core-activated
scenarios.description: activate: a 1x light (momentum 1.2) lights the core and wins.

scenarios.name: enemy-stalker-alone
scenarios.description: A stalker wakes on beat 1 and hunts the only self.

scenarios.name: enemy-stalker-farthest
scenarios.description: A stalker hunts the FARTHEST self past a nearer one, kills it on its beat grid, then re-picks the survivor.

scenarios.name: enemy-shielder-alone-clangs
scenarios.description: One self alone can never hurt a shielder: eight lights all clang off the shield.

scenarios.name: enemy-shielder-pair-hit
scenarios.description: A pops the shield, B follows inside the window and lands; the shield is back at once, so A’s next swing only pops it again.

scenarios.name: enemy-shielder-two-pairs-kill
scenarios.description: Two coordinated pairs kill it: B’s landed hit shoves it toward C, who supplies the second follow-up after A pops it again.

scenarios.name: enemy-shielder-same-substep-kill
scenarios.description: Two selves strike on the same substep with 1x heavies: the first pops, the second kills (the classic two-self kill).

scenarios.name: enemy-shielder-blocks-bolts
scenarios.description: A self hides behind a shielder from a turret: the bolts clang off the shield without popping it.

scenarios.name: enemy-brute-three-lights
scenarios.description: Three standing 1x lights kill a brute; the first two neither move nor stagger it (poise).

scenarios.name: enemy-brute-poise-broken
scenarios.description: A 2x standing heavy (momentum 4) is above the brute’s poise: it really moves and staggers it.

scenarios.name: enemy-grunt-shoved
scenarios.description: The same light that a brute shrugs off shoves a grunt back.

scenarios.name: enemy-brute-running-heavy
scenarios.description: One 1x running heavy (approach clamps to 1: momentum 3) kills a brute outright.

scenarios.name: enemy-brute-slam-wide
scenarios.description: An awake brute telegraphs its slam and lands it on its grid beat; the slam is wide enough to kill a self at its side as well.

scenarios.name: enemy-brute-holds-heavy-plate
scenarios.description: A sleeping brute’s body holds a heavy plate.

scenarios.name: enemy-drone-backs-off
scenarios.description: A drone backs off from a self that is too close until it is at its keep distance.

scenarios.name: enemy-drone-hovers-over-void
scenarios.description: A drone closes in over a void trench and a low barrier that would stop a walker.

scenarios.name: enemy-drone-fire
scenarios.description: A drone fires telegraphed bolts on the off-beat along its locked aim at three spread-out selves.

scenarios.name: enemy-drone-two-hits
scenarios.description: A drone takes two hit points: a 2x light (2 damage) kills it.

scenarios.name: boss-coordinated-win
scenarios.description: One self holds the boss’s eye in front, another lands 2x heavies on its back: phases 2 and 3, then the kill; both survive.

scenarios.name: boss-alone-armour
scenarios.description: One self alone can never hurt the boss (armour clangs) and is cleaved on the bar grid.

scenarios.name: boss-phases
scenarios.description: Two back hits move the boss to phase 2 (adds the sweep ring of shock shots) and phase 3 (attacks every two beats).

scenarios.name: boss-memory-none
scenarios.description: First take, no memory: only the base pattern; the pillar shelters tape A.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-dwell
scenarios.description: With memory of committed tape A the boss pre-empts A’s remembered dwell: telegraphed at the remembered place, then struck.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-blind-armour
scenarios.description: Without memory, B is the nearest self, holds the boss’s attention and clangs off its armour.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-exploited
scenarios.description: With memory, the boss commits to punishing A’s old spot and B’s back hit lands.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-guard-cancels
scenarios.description: A strong back hit during the recall telegraph staggers the boss and cancels the memory strike, protecting the remembered tape.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-attack-recall
scenarios.description: A remembered attack (a light swung while passing) is pre-empted on the nearest whole beat.

scenarios.name: boss-memory-record
scenarios.description: Recording take B (idle) with memory of committed tape A sees the same memory strike as its authoritative resolve.

scenarios.name: ranged-pierce-line
scenarios.description: A piercing shot strikes three enemies in its line, each exactly once, then ends at the far wall.

scenarios.name: ranged-pierce-1-stops
scenarios.description: pierce 1 passes through one enemy and stops at the next.

scenarios.name: ranged-phase-through-wall
scenarios.description: A phase shot passes a full wall and kills the enemy behind it.

scenarios.name: ranged-phase-map-edge
scenarios.description: A long-range phase shot stops at the map edge.

scenarios.name: ranged-burst-wall
scenarios.description: A burst is stopped by a full wall: every pellet breaks on it.

scenarios.name: ranged-arc-over-wall
scenarios.description: An arc shot is lobbed over a full wall and lands on the enemy behind it.

scenarios.name: ranged-arc-blast
scenarios.description: An arc shot flies over a near enemy, lands at its range and its blast strikes every enemy it overlaps, pushing each away from the centre.

scenarios.name: ranged-arc-min-range
scenarios.description: A short arc shot never lands closer than its minRange.

scenarios.name: ranged-burst-fan
scenarios.description: A burst fans five pellets across 40°; pellets reach enemies on the fan’s edges but fizzle before a far one.

scenarios.name: ranged-momentum-model
scenarios.description: A ranged hit delivers def.impact through the melee damage / knockback / stagger arithmetic (efficiencies 1, the damage mod applies).

scenarios.name: ranged-door-blocks-straight-shot
scenarios.description: A closed door stops a straight shot.

scenarios.name: ranged-reverse-pass-fires-again
scenarios.description: A reverse tape fires again on every pass with the recorded direction, and each shot that arrives hurts again.

scenarios.name: missile-scenario-f-alone
scenarios.description: Scenario F: alone, the missile locks the nearest enemy (g1) at launch and strikes it.

scenarios.name: missile-scenario-f-target-change
scenarios.description: Scenario F: tape B knocks g2 closer before A’s launch; the same recorded launch locks g2 instead.

scenarios.name: missile-no-retarget
scenarios.description: After launch the missile never retargets, even when another enemy is shoved nearer to it.

scenarios.name: missile-target-dies-first
scenarios.description: When its target dies first the missile flies straight on and still never switches.

scenarios.name: missile-turn-rate
scenarios.description: A missile fired away from the only enemy turns round no faster than its turn rate and strikes it.

scenarios.name: missile-no-enemy-straight
scenarios.description: With no enemy the missile flies straight along the recorded direction until it breaks on the wall.

scenarios.name: ranged-ghost-launch-gating
scenarios.description: The recording ghost’s missile flies and kills the turret in its own take; under playback the self dies at the same moment and its ghost fires nothing.

scenarios.name: ranged-desynced-launches-nothing
scenarios.description: A self desynced at a shut door launches nothing.

scenarios.name: ranged-synced-launches
scenarios.description: Control: with the door open the same tape launches its missile.

scenarios.name: ability-manual-desync-record
scenarios.description: manualDesync live: the first press desyncs in place and holds the spark; the second re-syncs the body where it is. Replayed, the released spark must catch up by ordinary spark rules.

scenarios.name: ability-manual-desync-turret
scenarios.description: While voluntarily desynced the self is harmless and invulnerable: a turret never shoots at it.

scenarios.name: ability-manual-desync-paired
scenarios.description: An involuntary desync (a beat-timed door) is held by the next press, so recorded on/off presses stay paired.

scenarios.name: desync-beat-door
scenarios.description: Control: without the gear the same tape resyncs as soon as the beat-timed door opens.

scenarios.name: ability-low-profile
scenarios.description: lowProfile: a self 9 tiles from a turret (reach 12) is read as 13.5 tiles away and never shot.

scenarios.name: ability-low-profile-control
scenarios.description: Control: without lowProfile the same self is shot.

scenarios.name: ability-loudmouth
scenarios.description: loudmouth: a self 14 tiles from a turret is read as 10.5 tiles away and shot.

scenarios.name: ability-beat-sight
scenarios.description: beatSight: upcoming enemy attack beats (8-beat look-ahead) are listed in every sampled snapshot (threatBeats) and match the beats the turret’s shots land on.

scenarios.name: ability-phase-dodge-record
scenarios.description: phaseDodge: a dodge passes through a column of low barriers live and replays without desync.

scenarios.name: ability-phase-dodge-blocked
scenarios.description: Without phaseDodge the same dodge is stopped by the barrier while recording.

scenarios.name: ability-phase-dodge-replayed-without-gear
scenarios.description: The phased tape replayed without the gear cannot cross the barrier: it desyncs there.

scenarios.name: ability-slide-strike
scenarios.description: slideStrike: a strike started straight out of a dodge carries extra momentum, only on a forward pass of a reverse tape.

scenarios.name: ability-parry
scenarios.description: parry: a heavy swing turns an enemy shot inside its arc back at the shooter; the reflected bolt destroys the turret.

scenarios.name: ability-parry-control
scenarios.description: Control: without the gear the same swing does nothing to the shot, which kills.

scenarios.name: ability-kill-refresh
scenarios.description: killRefresh: a melee kill by the live self refunds its dodge cooldown, so the second dodge press (tick 26) is accepted.

scenarios.name: ability-kill-refresh-control
scenarios.description: Control: without the gear the second dodge press falls inside the cooldown and is dropped.

scenarios.name: gear-ranged-mixtape-rocket
scenarios.description: Catalogue ranged weapon mixtape_rocket (missile): the live self steps forward and fires twice down a room of sleeping grunts; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-ranged-needle-rail
scenarios.description: Catalogue ranged weapon needle_rail (pierce): the live self steps forward and fires twice down a room of sleeping grunts; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-ranged-bleed-emitter
scenarios.description: Catalogue ranged weapon bleed_emitter (phase): the live self steps forward and fires twice down a room of sleeping grunts; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-ranged-bass-drop
scenarios.description: Catalogue ranged weapon bass_drop (arc): the live self steps forward and fires twice down a room of sleeping grunts; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-ranged-static-spray
scenarios.description: Catalogue ranged weapon static_spray (burst): the live self steps forward and fires twice down a room of sleeping grunts; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-splice-blade
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon splice_blade: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-stylus-shiv
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon stylus_shiv: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-amp-sledge
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon amp_sledge: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-reel-lash
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon reel_lash: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-speaker-knuckles
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon speaker_knuckles: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-melee-vinyl-glaive
scenarios.description: Catalogue melee weapon vinyl_glaive: the live self walks up to a tough sleeping grunt and swings light and heavy, standing and running; recorded from inputs, then resolved.

scenarios.name: gear-apparel-mods
scenarios.description: Apparel stat mods combined (moveSpeed, accel, momentumRetention, approachBonus, meleeImpact, dodgeIframes, sparkSpeed): the live self runs, turns, dodges and lands a running heavy on a grunt.

scenarios.name: gear-abilities-catalogue
scenarios.description: Catalogue ability gear (dropout_jacket manualDesync, slick_sliders slideStrike, click_visor beatSight): the live self dodges into a slide strike, then desyncs and re-syncs on demand while a turret looks for it.

scenarios.name: trap-spikes
scenarios.description: Spikes on a beat window kill a playback self standing on a raised cell (and only there), publish their id to a door and telegraph a beat ahead; always-raised spikes kill a grunt on contact, hit a brute once per beat and clang off a shielder.

scenarios.name: trap-spikes-dodge
scenarios.description: A recorded dodge carries a playback self across a quarter-beat spike window; the same path one row down without the dodge dies inside the window.

scenarios.name: trap-spikes-live
scenarios.description: Raised spikes kill the live self once; the recording ghost then walks on over them freely.

scenarios.name: trap-crusher-stroke
scenarios.description: A piston across the room strokes on its beat window: it crushes the self and the enemies on its cells (drone included), pushes a 5 hp survivor out, only walls off a self beside it, and desyncs a self that dodged the stroke on a cell.

scenarios.name: trap-crusher-desync-recover
scenarios.description: A playback self walking into an extended piston desyncs ("blocked by crusher cr"); its spark waits at the face and resyncs once the retract completes.

scenarios.name: trap-crusher-live-hold
scenarios.description: The live self standing in a piston lane is crushed on the stroke and its body is pushed out; the signal returns mid-retract, so the piston re-extends without a second stroke.

scenarios.name: trap-flame
scenarios.description: A flame jet is cut short by a closed door and burns the self behind it the moment another tape opens the door; a second jet stops at an extended crusher and passes a low barrier; a third burns a turret, a drone and a brute once per beat.

scenarios.name: trap-conveyor
scenarios.description: Belts carry a sleeping grunt in master time and reverse on a switch (publishing <id>.rev to a door); turrets, drones and playback selves are never carried; a body is stopped by a wall, not pushed through it; a belt with runWhen stops and starts.

scenarios.name: trap-conveyor-dart-drift
scenarios.description: A dart crossing a belt that runs across its lane drifts sideways with the belt without turning.

scenarios.name: trap-conveyor-live-ride
scenarios.description: The live self is carried by a belt by what the world moves per local tick (1x take, then a 2x take after a later tape reversed the belt); the rides are baked into the tapes and replay unchanged.

scenarios.name: trap-bumper
scenarios.description: Bumpers fire once per rising edge: a grunt is thrown the full power with real knockback, a brute by power / mass, a turret and a recorded self not at all, and a grunt thrown into a wall staggers.

scenarios.name: trap-bumper-live
scenarios.description: A bumper throws the live self (1x take, then a 2x take standing on the same plate); the flights are recorded as ordinary movement and replay without the plate.

scenarios.name: trap-magnet
scenarios.description: A magnet drags enemies in range toward its centre at pull / mass and holds them short of it (turret never, a far grunt never, selves never); a beat-driven magnet pulls a drone only while on.

scenarios.name: trap-dart
scenarios.description: Dart launchers fire on their beat grids, never aim: the first vulnerable self in a lane is shot and the next dart flies through its ghost to the self behind; darts strike a grunt and then a brute behind it (1 damage each, credited to the launcher); offset and enabledWhen gate a third launcher.

scenarios.name: trap-dart-crusher
scenarios.description: An extended crusher stops darts at its face and a crusher plugging the muzzle stops the launcher firing at all.

scenarios.name: trap-dart-dodge-parry
scenarios.description: A dart passes through a self inside recorded dodge i-frames; with parry, a heavy swing turns another launcher's dart like any enemy shot.

scenarios.name: trap-sensor
scenarios.description: Beam sensors: a self crossing a beam trips it (and a door on it starts opening that substep); a latched beam stays on; an enemies-only beam ignores the self; a beam cut by a closed door sees the grunt before the door, not the one beyond.

scenarios.name: trap-sensor-relay-chain
scenarios.description: A belt carries a grunt through an enemies-only tripwire: the door on the wire starts opening that substep and a relay (quantize 1, delay 1) fires a crusher onto the grunt exactly one beat after the next beat.

scenarios.name: trap-relay-modes
scenarios.description: Relays turn a switch into a pulse (next beat, one beat), a quantize-2 / delay-1 / half-beat pulse, an immediate quarter-beat pulse, a latch and a toggle; a hold-2 relay ignores triggers while armed or pulsing and publishes <id>.armed; a delay-1 relay gives the crusher it drives a full one-beat telegraph.

scenarios.name: trap-machines-vs-enemies
scenarios.description: Machines turned against enemies: a belt delivers a sleeping grunt into a recorded swing, and a 0.5x swing too weak to hurt shoves a grunt into a dart lane where the next dart kills it.

scenarios.name: trap-spikes-hunter
scenarios.description: An awake grunt hunting a self walks onto raised spikes and dies: the trap does not care who it is.

scenarios.name: trap-gauntlet
scenarios.description: One of every machine with awake enemies in one room; two live takes (1x wandering with every action, then 2x) recorded through the player controller and resolved: everything interacts.

scenarios.name: sandbox-bot-solo
scenarios.description: The shipped sandbox level with the baseline loadout: one 1x take opens the gate, clears both grunts and the turret while dodging its bolt (bot inputs, recorded open-loop).

scenarios.name: sandbox-bot-two-cassettes
scenarios.description: The sandbox with two cassettes: A (1x) opens the door and holds the plate, B (2x) fights.
